title: Outil de prise en charge COVID-19 au service des urgences (ED) de l'ACEP
short_title: Outil de prise en charge COVID-19 au service des urgences (ED) de l'ACEP
abbreviations: ACEP ED COVID-19 Management Tool, ACEP
formula:
[Recommandations pour le bilan :](https://www.acep.org/globalassets/sites/acep/media/covid-19-main/acep-covid-19-ed-management-tool.pdf)

[Recommandations pour le traitement :](https://www.acep.org/corona/COVID-19-alert/covid-19-articles/covid-19-ED-management-tool-now-available/)

![](https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/cdn-web-img.mdcalc.com/acep-covid19-2024-non-pharm-tx.png)

how_to_use.why: Cet algorithme fournit un cadre pragmatique pour standardiser la classification de la gravité, l’évaluation du risque, le bilan diagnostique, l’orientation et le traitement des patients adultes chez qui une infection par le SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) est suspectée ou confirmée.
how_to_use.when: Pour guider la classification de la gravité, la stratification du risque, ainsi que les décisions diagnostiques et de prise en charge chez les patients adultes (≥18 ans) présentant une infection suspectée ou confirmée à SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) au service des urgences.
how_to_use.pearls:
- This algorithm is not intended as a substitute for clinicians' clinical judgement.
- This algorithm is not exhaustive in regards to diagnostic and treatment recommendations for patients with COVID-19 and COVID-like illness.
- Patients presenting with symptoms conditions that may be manifestations of COVID-19 may also be manifestations of other serious disease (e.g. MI, PE, stroke), requiring additional specific diagnostic and therapeutic interventions not discussed in this tool.
- This ACEP ED COVID-19 Management Tool was funded in part by a cooperative agreement with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention ([grant number 1 NU50CK000570](https://taggs.hhs.gov/Detail/AwardDetail?arg_AwardNum=NU50CK000570&arg_ProgOfficeCode=252)). The CDC is an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The contents of this ACEP tool do not necessarily represent the policy of CDC or HHS and should not be considered an endorsement by the Federal Government.

next_steps.advice: Patients presenting with symptoms conditions that may be manifestations of severe or critical COVID-19 may also be manifestations of other diseases (e.g. MI, PE, stroke), requiring additional specific diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Il n'est pas nécessaire d'appliquer cet outil aux patients qui ne sont pas évalués pour la COVID-19.
- Si le patient est considéré comme atteint d'une forme légère, cet outil peut aider à éviter des examens complémentaires.
next_steps.management:
- Refer to step 5 of the[ACEP ED COVID-19 Management Tool](https://www.acep.org/globalassets/sites/acep/media/covid-19-main/acep-covid-19-ed-management-tool.pdf)for pharmacologic treatment recommendations.
- Imaging, lab tests, treatment and disposition should be considered based on severity and risk for disease progression.
- ACEP maintains information on laboratoratory findings at hospital admission, laboratory abnormalities in severe disease, and hypercoaguability in the[ACEP COVID-19 Field Guide](https://www.acep.org/corona/covid-19-field-guide/assessment/laboratory-abnormalities/)section on laboratory abnormalities.
- The[CDC](https://archive.cdc.gov/#/details?url=https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/covid-data/investigations-discovery/hospitalization-death-by-race-ethnicity.html)has more information on how race, ethnicity, and access to health care resources may affect outcomes.
- [AJOG](https://www.ajog.org/article/S0002-9378(21)00033-8/fulltext)has published a guideline to assist with risk stratification of pregnant patients.
- NIH guidance for COVID-19 is no longer available as of August 2024. An archive version of the guidance can be found[here](https://archive.org/details/covid-19-treatment-guidelines/mode/2up).
- Clinical recommendations are still maintained by some medical societies such as the[IDSA](https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/covid-19-guideline-treatment-and-management/)and[ACEP](https://www.acep.org/corona/covid-19-Main).

evidence:
All current citations are listed on page 5 of the Emergency Department COVID-19 Management Tool. Summary of references as below:

**Step 1 - Severity Classification**

The disease severity classification utilized by this tool (Mild, Moderate, Severe, Critical) is based upon that adopted by the National Institute of Health COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines Panel which in turn is based upon an early consensus of the literature describing the disease entity initially presenting in Wuhan, China, and subsequently identified as SARS-CoV-2.

**Step 2 - Diagnostic Testing and Interpretation**

This section follows previous NIH guidelines for testing recommendations. Evidence for exertional O2 measurement is included from (Greenhalgh 2020, Goodacre 2020, Paglia 2020).

It is recommended to utilize ACEP’s COVID-19 Field Guide section on[abnormal lab values](https://www.acep.org/corona/covid-19-field-guide/assessment/laboratory-abnormalities)to review lab results.

**Step 3 - Disposition**

This section lays out appropriate disposition of the patient based on their severity classification. Most of this section was devised from consensus among the working group. Supplemental evidence was included from Banerjee 2021, links to previous patient educational materials from the CDC, and multiple helpful links for patients from JAMA (example:[https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/2763176](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/2763176)).

**Step 4 - Non-Pharmacologic Treatment**

This section cites 8 references which include non-pharmacologic treatment of respiratory infections in general (e.g. Patchett 2021) as well as COVID-19 specifically (e.g. Banerjee 2021). It also includes a review of treatments for outpatient and inpatient COVID-19 management. The recommendations are listed, based upon provider assessment of disease severity. Some of these recommendations are consensus-based.

**Step 5 - Pharmacologic Treatment**

This section is abstracted directly from the previously available NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines, which are mainly evidence-based. The entries are listed by severity of disease. When provided in the NIH guidelines, the strength of the recommendation and level of evidence for the recommendation are specified. For example, for moderate, severe and critical COVID-19, the following is provided:

- Remdesivir: For hospitalized patients who require minimal supplemental oxygen (BIIa).

**Optional Step - Risk Prognostication**

This step utilizes the PRIEST Score as a validated tool to predict a patient’s risk for end organ failure and/or mortality. It was a mixed prospective and retrospective observational cohort study in 70 emergency departments across the United Kingdom (UK). 22,445 patients were included who were suspected to have COVID-19 between 26 March 2020 and 28 May 2020. This tool was included because it did not require diagnostic testing (labs, imaging) as part of the evaluation of the patient. ([https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7822515/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7822515/)).

**Optional Step - Risk Assessment**

Additional risk factors that could increase the patient’s risk for severe disease, organ failure, and/or mortality can also be considered when evaluating a patient with COVID-19. The CDC[previously](https://archive.cdc.gov/#/details?url=https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/covid-data/investigations-discovery/hospitalization-death-by-race-ethnicity.html)maintained information regarding risk associated with race/ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and healthcare resources. Additional references (Bellou 2020, Ebinger 2020, Lokken 2021, Strausz 2021, Williamson 2020, Tartof 2020) are included that summarize evidence for other risk factors.
